exact_version: Steven Savitt, Being and Becoming in Modern Physics, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Fall 2021 archive edition (minor correction; page says substantive revision 2017-08-21).
locator: Secs. 3.2, especially archived page lines 256-265; author and citation information page for edition identity.
quote: The relation is that between a point x and each point in or on its past light cone.
read_scope: Read the archived SEP entry's Stein discussion and its author/citation page. Secondary exposition only; Stein 1968 itself was not read in this run.
findings: The SEP entry supports the stated secondary account: it describes a relation defined by the past light cone, explains the reflexive/transitive/unsettled conditions, and presents the result as a formal response to the Rietdijk-Putnam-Penrose argument conditional on accepting this relation as becoming. The record's exact version is the Fall 2021 archive, but its claim that a substantive revision occurred 2021-10-06 is wrong: the archived entry says substantive revision 2017-08-21; SEP's edition metadata identifies Fall 2021 as a minor correction. Keep the SEP's secondary status explicit; it does not verify Stein's primary theorem.
downgrade_proposal: Correct the version date to Fall 2021 archive (minor correction) and note the page's 2017-08-21 substantive-revision date. Keep read_depth at full-text only as a full reading of the secondary SEP entry; do not treat it as primary-text verification.
contracts_affected: RC-2 contextual secondary source only; it cannot establish the primary Stein result or replace found-stein-1991/found-malament-1977

exact_version: Nathan Madsen, arXiv:2607.05840v1 [gr-qc], submitted 2026-07-07 (HTML identifies v1).
quote: their interiors are related by an ε-approximate isometry
read_scope: Targeted full-text audit of abstract, Definition 2.6, Theorems 4.18 and 5.1, Corollary 5.6, and discussion. The full proofs and appendices were not audited.
findings: Author and version match the register. Theorem 4.18 proves approximate isometry on deep interiors for a finite causal set with two well-conditioned embeddings into globally hyperbolic d-dimensional Lorentzian manifolds, subject to the stated density/curvature-scale bound; Definition 2.6 includes exact order preservation, scale-dependent density control, and longest-chain/proper-time correspondence. Theorem 5.1 is the separate Poisson-sprinkling probability result, and Corollary 5.6 combines it for two embeddings. The record's formulas and stated conditions match the located text at statement level. This is a reconstruction result for completed causal sets and supplies no result about growth, becoming, or observers. The frozen frame identifies this record as the same paper as frontier-causal-embedding-2026, an RC-4 alias; that scope does not make it evidence for growth or becoming.
downgrade_proposal: None for the checked statement-level claims. Preserve the existing limitation that this is not a proof audit or a result about temporal ontology.
contracts_affected: RC-4 alias of frontier-causal-embedding-2026; this completed-causet reconstruction result supplies no support for the contract's becoming claim.

findings: The arXiv v3 text identifies Bernal and Sánchez and states Theorem 1.1 for globally hyperbolic spacetimes, yielding a smooth product splitting with a Cauchy temporal function; Theorem 1.2 states that a spacetime admitting a time function admits a temporal function. locator: Abstract; Secs. 2-4; Sec. 6 on quantum equilibrium; Sec. 7 discussion.
quote: seem to qualify as fundamentally Lorentz invariant
read_scope: Targeted full-text audit of the abstract and sections 2-4, 6-7. No derivation of empirical-equivalence results was reproduced.
findings: The authors, version, and journal metadata match. The paper says multi-particle relativistic Bohmian dynamics requires a privileged foliation in the usual formulation, and proposes extracting one covariantly from the wave function; its conclusion remains explicitly hedged. Sec. 3 says a vector field must be integrable to define orthogonal foliation leaves and warns its integrable part may cease to be timelike. The register captures these qualifications. Its quantum-equilibrium/standard-prediction claim is conditional on equilibrium along the chosen foliation, not a proof that every covariant formulation has standard predictions.
downgrade_proposal: None for the checked claims. Retain the scope restriction to the paper's formulations and its authors' evaluative, hedged Lorentz-invariance claim.

locator: Secs. 3.1-3.4; Sec. 4.1-4.3, especially Eqs. (21)-(23); Sec. 5.1 and 5.3.
quote: the thermal time evolution corresponds to a translation in the global time coordinate
read_scope: Targeted full-text audit of the construction, kappa- and rho-Minkowski examples, conclusion, and open-problem statements. Formal C*-algebra existence and derivations were not independently audited.
findings: The author, title, and v1 version match. The paper defines the spacetime integral as a weight that cannot be normalized as a state on the infinite-volume model; it constructs modular/KMS flow from the momentum-space modular function. For kappa-Minkowski, Eq. (22) gives a global x0 translation with factor d/kappa, and the paper notes the flow is not kappa-Poincare invariant. For rho-Minkowski it reports a unimodular case with trivial modular evolution and relates it to discrete time. It marks inner-automorphism freedom and phenomenology as open/speculative. The record's broad claims are supported, provided the thermal-time hypothesis and model-specific formal setting remain explicit.
downgrade_proposal: None for the checked author claims. Keep read limitations: the flow is an algebraic construction for spacetime, not an operational observer clock; preserve the paper's caveats about non-normalizable weight, inner-automorphism freedom, and mathematical completion.

exact_version: James B. Hartle, arXiv:gr-qc/0403001v2, dated 2004-05-21; published Am. J. Phys. 73 (2005), 101-109, DOI 10.1119/1.1783900.
locator: Abstract; Sec. II (IGUS model); Sec. III (robot's present); Sec. IV; Sec. VI conclusion.
quote: Past, present, and future are not properties of four-dimensional spacetime
read_scope: Targeted full-text audit of the abstract, IGUS model, sections III-IV, conclusion, and cosmological-arrow appendix. No independent assessment of the cognitive model or its empirical testability.
findings: The author and arXiv v2 date match. Hartle presents simple information-gathering-and-utilizing-system models: the robot's present is stored data extending over intervals along its worldline, not a spacelike surface; he conjectures a subjective past-present-future organization may be adaptive for localized IGUSes. The record overstates the scope when it labels the assumed account a 'four-dimensional block description' and states as Hartle's conclusion that passage is not fundamental. The text offers a four-dimensional description of subjective temporal organization; it does not independently infer eternalism or settle objective passage. Treating the model as a block ontology is an interpretive bridge premise, not established by the cited passages.
downgrade_proposal: Rephrase the assumption as 'four-dimensional spacetime description of fundamental physics, used as the model framework'; label 'passage is not fundamental' as an interpretation/inference, not a direct result. Retain the author's narrower claim about IGUS processing and mark the cognitive-universal proposal as conjecture.

exact_version: Christian Wüthrich and Craig Callender, arXiv:1502.00018v1 [physics.hist-ph], submitted 30 January 2015; the versioned HTML identifies both authors as equal contributors.
locator: Sec. 3, especially paragraphs on genericity and Lorentz symmetry (arXiv HTML lines 109-116); Sec. 4, localized and global becoming discussion (lines 121-155); Sec. 5 conclusion.
quote: we suspect that large and many non-Hegelian subsets are few and far between
read_scope: Targeted full-text check of versioned arXiv HTML, including the counterexample relation, genericity qualification, Lorentz-symmetry discussion, and growth interpretation. Did not read cited Stein primary text or unpublished Meyer estimate; no numerical-statistical reproduction.
findings: The source version and author identity match. Section 3 explicitly constructs a finite causet counterexample to the CST analogue of Stein’s result: a reflexive, transitive, non-trivial, non-universal, automorphism-invariant relation can include a spacelike non-Hegelian pair in both directions. However, the record states too flatly that large non-Hegelian subsets are non-generic and regular ones violate Lorentz invariance. The authors acknowledge almost no relevant analytic or numerical results, present the scarcity claim as their suspicion, make the no-macroscopic-present conclusion conditional (“if this is right”), and infer detectable Lorentz violation for the highly regular structures. Section 4 further presents growth-compatible objective becoming as a philosophical proposal with costs, not an established physical result. This same-paper alias anchors RC-4 claims about causal-set becoming; the finite counterexample is stronger support than the uncertain population-level genericity argument.
downgrade_proposal: Keep the explicit finite counterexample as a checked source claim. Recast scarcity of sufficiently large/many non-Hegelian subsets as the authors' qualified conjecture/inference, with the unavailable published statistics and unpublished Meyer estimate stated; make the Lorentz-violation claim conditional on the relevant highly regular structures. Keep the proposed global becoming as philosophical compatibility, not physical establishment.
contracts_affected: RC-4 alias of frontier-causal-becoming-2015; downgrade only the genericity/Lorentz-inference support, not the checked finite counterexample or compatibility proposal.
